title: Maximize Active Section with Trade I
summary: Given a binary string s of length n , where '1' represents an active section and '0' represents an inactive section, you can perform at most one trade to maximize the number of active sections.
statement: Given a binary string s of length n , where '1' represents an active section and '0' represents an inactive section, you can perform at most one trade to maximize the number of active sections. In a trade, you can convert a contiguous block of '1's that is surrounded by '0's into all '0's, and convert a contiguous block of '0's that is surrounded by '1's into all '1's. The string s is augmented with '1's at both ends to form a new string t = '1' + s + '1' . The augmented '1's do not contribute to the final count. Return the maximum number of active sections in s after making the optimal trade.
constraints: s is a nonempty binary string, conceptually surrounded by inactive-external sentinel ones.
A trade removes a one-run surrounded by zeros, then activates a zero-run surrounded by ones.
Return the maximum active count after at most one trade; sentinels never count.
hints: Removing a one-run merges its adjacent zero-runs, and activating that merged run gains exactly their combined lengths.
Run-length encode the string and track consecutive zero-run lengths.
Count existing ones; for each zero run after another zero run, update the best sum of the pair separated by one-run.
Every legal trade corresponds to exactly two adjacent zero runs in the run sequence, and their intervening ones cancel from the net change.
editorial: Every legal trade corresponds to exactly two adjacent zero runs in the run sequence, and their intervening ones cancel from the net change.

tests.explanation: No beneficial complete trade exists, so the single active section remains.
Trading the middle one joins and activates both zero runs, producing five active positions.
